en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Tenth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether the Five Consciousnesses are Wholesome or Unwholesome:
Are the five consciousnesses wholesome or unwholesome?
Yes, they are.
Is it not the case that the five types of sensory consciousness have arisen bases and arisen objects?
Yes, they do.
If the five types of sensory consciousness have arisen bases and arisen objects, then indeed, you should not say—
“The five types of consciousness are both wholesome and unwholesome.
Is it not the case that the five types of consciousness have pre-arisen bases, have pre-arisen objects, have internal bases, have external objects,
have unmixed bases, have unmixed objects, have diverse bases, and have diverse objects, and do not share one another’s domain or sphere?
They experience [them]; they do not arise without attention, they do not arise without mental engagement, they do not arise without succession,
they do not arise neither before nor after, they do not arise one immediately after the other—
surely the fivefold sense-consciousnesses are effortless?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If the five types of sensory consciousness are effortless, then surely it should not be said that ‘the five types of sensory consciousness are both wholesome and unwholesome’?”
Is eye-consciousness wholesome? Yes.
Does eye-consciousness arise by taking emptiness as its object?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does eye-consciousness arise having emptiness as its object? Yes.
“Visual consciousness arises dependent on the eye and emptiness”?
One should not say so.
“Visual consciousness arises dependent on the eye and emptiness”? [One should not say so.]
“Yes,” [he] says.
“Is there such a sutta as: ‘Dependent upon the eye and emptiness, eye-consciousness arises’?”
"There is not.
"The discourse stating, 'Dependent upon the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises'—
does such a sutta exist?"
“Yes,” [he replies].
“If it is true that there is such a sutta as ‘Dependent on the eye and forms,
eye-consciousness arises,’ then indeed, sir, you should not say:”
“Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and emptiness.
Is eye-consciousness both wholesome and unwholesome? Yes.
Does eye-consciousness arise by taking the past or the future as its object?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Is eye-consciousness both wholesome and unwholesome?
“Yes.
Eye-consciousness arises conditioned by contact … conditioned by mind … conditioned by the eye … [and so on].
Does it arise contingent upon the body … contingent upon sound … [and so on] … contingent upon the tangible?
One should not say so … [and so on].
Is mental consciousness both wholesome and unwholesome, and does mental consciousness arise having emptiness as its object? Yes.
Is eye-consciousness both wholesome and unwholesome, and does eye-consciousness arise having emptiness as its object?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is mental consciousness both wholesome and unwholesome? Is mental consciousness arisen by taking as its object the past and the future? Yes.
Is eye-consciousness both wholesome and unwholesome? Is eye-consciousness that arises by taking as its object the past or the future?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...is mind-consciousness both wholesome and unwholesome? Is mind-consciousness [arising] by taking contact as its object... [and so on]?
Does it arise by taking mind as its object … pe … by taking body as its object … by taking sound as its object … pe … by taking tangible object as its object?
“Yes.
“Is eye-consciousness both wholesome and unwholesome? Does eye-consciousness arise by taking contact as its object … [and so on] … by taking tangible objects as its object?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “the fivefold sense-consciousness is both wholesome and unwholesome”?
“Yes, [it is so].
“But was it not said by the Blessed One:
‘Here, monks, having seen a form with the eye, a monk grasps at its signs …’?”
He does not grasp at signs ... pe ...
having heard a sound with the ear ... pe ...
having touched a tangible object with the body, he grasps at signs ... pe ...
“He does not grasp at signs.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
Therefore, the fivefold sense-consciousnesses are both wholesome and unwholesome.
The discussion that the fivefold sense-consciousnesses are both wholesome and unwholesome is concluded.
